question: Is the elevated eQTL false-discovery rate reproducible, and which assumptions or reference distributions explain it?
disclosure: All cohorts are synthetic. Existing published results and scientific sources remain unchanged.

responses: Log2 CPM without the plus-one offset
diagnostic_bank.purpose: Paired response ablations on exactly the same generated cohorts. The latent response is an oracle diagnostic unavailable in real data.

validation_bank.wild_distribution: Independent participant-level Rademacher multipliers shared across genes and hypotheses in a cohort
validation_bank.p_value: (1 + bootstrap statistics at least as large as the observed statistic)/(999 + 1)
validation_bank.purpose: Independent size and strong-signal power validation. No cutoff is tuned from this bank. Wild bootstrap inference remains approximate.

multiplicity: BH 0.05 applied separately to each family, as in the original study. No joint guarantee across families.
multiplicity_diagnostics: Also report marginal nominal rejection, Bonferroni family rejection and BY family rejection on the same P values. These distinguish marginal P-value calibration from family adjustment; they are not outcome-tuned cutoffs.
diagnostics: Cohort-level false discoveries and Monte Carlo uncertainty
reporting: Wilson 95 percent intervals for all-null cohort rejection, mean FDP and simulation standard errors for partial alternatives. Report all specified cells; do not discard unfavourable seeds or retune thresholds.
policy: Lock source hashes before fresh evaluation. Preserve old results. Any algorithmic correction must be recorded and affected new runs repeated. Existing small-bank tests are post hoc, and multiple-cell selection must be considered.
